shipping.question: What are your shipping options?
shipping.answer: We offer standard shipping (5-7 business days), express shipping (2-3 business days), and next-day delivery for select areas. Free standard shipping is available on orders over $50.

returns.question: What is your return policy?
returns.answer: We accept returns within 30 days of purchase. Items must be unused and in their original packaging. Simply contact our support team to initiate a return and receive a prepaid shipping label.

tracking.question: How can I track my order?
tracking.answer: Once your order ships, you'll receive an email with a tracking number. You can also view your order status anytime by logging into your account and visiting the order history section.

international.question: Do you offer international shipping?
international.answer: Yes! We ship to over 50 countries worldwide. International shipping rates and delivery times vary by location. You can see the exact cost at checkout before completing your purchase.

resistorColorCode.noMatch: No standard band combination found for this value.
resistorColorCode.reverseFound: Closest match: {value}. Click Apply bands to use these colors.
resistorColorCode.educationTitle: How to read resistor color codes
resistorColorCode.educationBody: Resistor bodies use colored bands to encode resistance value, tolerance, and sometimes temperature coefficient. Read digits left to right, apply the multiplier, then check the tolerance band. A 4-band resistor uses two digits, a multiplier, and tolerance; 5- and 6-band types add a third digit and optional temperature coefficient band for precision parts.

ohmsLaw.title: Ohm's Law Calculator
ohmsLaw.description: Enter any two known values to calculate voltage, current, resistance, and power with unit conversion.

meta.title: Ohm's Law Calculator
meta.description: Calculate voltage, current, resistance, and power from any two known values at {siteName}.

ohmsLaw.hint: Lock two fields with known values; the other two are calculated automatically.
ohmsLaw.invalidCombination: Could not solve with the current combination of values.
ohmsLaw.educationBody: Ohm's law relates voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R): V = I × R. Power (P) is the rate of energy transfer: P = V × I. Given any two quantities, the others can be derived — essential for sizing resistors, checking LED current, and debugging circuits.

voltageDivider.title: Voltage Divider Calculator
voltageDivider.description: Enter any three values to solve for the fourth in a classic two-resistor voltage divider.

meta.title: Voltage Divider Calculator
meta.description: Calculate output voltage, resistor values, and divider current for no-load circuits at {siteName}.

voltageDivider.hint: Enter any three values; the fourth is calculated automatically.
voltageDivider.voutExceedsVin: Output voltage must be less than input voltage.
voltageDivider.invalidCombination: Enter exactly three positive values to solve.
voltageDivider.educationBody: A voltage divider uses two series resistors to produce a lower output voltage: Vout = Vin × R2 / (R1 + R2). The same current flows through both resistors. This calculator assumes no load on the output — real circuits may need a buffer if the load draws significant current.

seriesParallel.title: Series & Parallel Resistor Calculator
seriesParallel.description: Add up to 10 resistors and calculate the equivalent resistance for series or parallel circuits.

meta.title: Series & Parallel Resistor Calculator
meta.description: Calculate equivalent resistance for up to 10 resistors in series or parallel at {siteName}.

seriesParallel.hint: Choose series or parallel mode, enter resistor values, and view the equivalent resistance.
seriesParallel.invalidCombination: Enter at least one positive resistor value.
seriesParallel.educationBody: In series, resistances add: Req = R1 + R2 + … + Rn. In parallel, reciprocals add: 1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + … + 1/Rn. Series circuits share the same current; parallel circuits share the same voltage across each branch.

smdCode.title: SMD Resistor Code Calculator
smdCode.description: Decode 3-digit, 4-digit, and EIA-96 SMD markings to resistance values — or find all matching codes from a value.

meta.title: SMD Resistor Code Calculator
meta.description: Decode and encode 3-digit, 4-digit, and EIA-96 SMD resistor markings at {siteName}.

smdCode.hint: Select a marking type, then decode a code or enter a resistance value to find possible markings.
smdCode.invalidCode: Invalid code for the selected marking type.
smdCode.noMatch: No matching SMD code found for this value.

reference.3digit: 3-digit codes use two significant digits followed by a power-of-ten multiplier. Example: 472 = 47 × 10² = 4.7 kΩ.
reference.4digit: 4-digit codes use three significant digits followed by a multiplier. Example: 1001 = 100 × 10¹ = 1 kΩ.
reference.eia96: EIA-96 uses a two-digit value code (01–96) from a standard table, followed by a letter multiplier (Z through F).

smdCode.educationBody: Surface-mount resistors often use printed codes instead of color bands. 3- and 4-digit markings encode significant digits and a decimal multiplier; EIA-96 uses a compact two-digit plus letter system for 1% tolerance parts. Always confirm package size and manufacturer tolerance when ordering replacements.

timer555.title: 555 Timer Calculator
timer555.description: Calculate astable frequency, period, and duty cycle, or monostable pulse width from resistor and capacitor values.

meta.title: 555 Timer Calculator
meta.description: Calculate 555 timer astable and monostable timing from R and C values at {siteName}.

timer555.hint: Select astable or monostable mode and enter resistor and capacitor values with units.
timer555.educationBody: The NE555 is a versatile timer IC. In astable mode it oscillates continuously: frequency depends on R1, R2, and C. In monostable mode it produces a single timed pulse when triggered. These formulas assume ideal components and the standard bipolar 555; actual timing may vary slightly with supply voltage and temperature.
